source.text: וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר נִבְנְתָה֙ הַחוֹמָ֔ה וָאַעֲמִ֖יד הַדְּלָת֑וֹת וַיִּפָּֽקְד֛וּ הַשּׁוֹעֲרִ֥ים וְהַמְשֹׁרְרִ֖ים וְהַלְוִיִּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was when had been built the wall and I had set up the doors, and were appointed the gatekeepers and the singers and the Levites,

en.L: And it was, when the wall had been built and I had set up the doors, and the gatekeepers and the singers and the Levites had been appointed,
en.B: When the wall had been rebuilt and I had set the doors in place, and the gatekeepers, the singers and the Levites had been appointed to their duties,
en.R: The wall was now rebuilt, and I had hung the doors in the gateways. The gatekeepers, the singers and the Levites were given their jobs.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando el muro había sido edificado y yo había colocado las puertas, y habían sido designados los porteros y los cantores y los levitas,
es.B: Cuando ya se había reconstruido el muro y yo había puesto las puertas en su lugar, y se había asignado su servicio a los porteros, los cantores y los levitas,
es.R: El muro ya estaba reconstruido, y yo había colocado las puertas en las entradas. A los porteros, los cantores y los levitas se les asignaron sus tareas.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand la muraille eut été bâtie et que j’eus dressé les battants, et que les portiers et les chanteurs et les Lévites eurent été établis,
fr.B: Lorsque la muraille fut rebâtie, que j’eus mis en place les battants des portes et que les portiers, les chanteurs et les Lévites eurent été affectés à leurs fonctions,
fr.R: La muraille était maintenant rebâtie, et j’avais posé les battants des portes. Les portiers, les chanteurs et les Lévites ont reçu leurs tâches.

sw.L: Ikawa, ukuta ulipokwisha kujengwa, nami nilipokwisha kuisimamisha milango, na mabawabu na waimbaji na Walawi walipokwisha kuwekwa,
sw.B: Ukuta ulipokwisha kujengwa upya, nami nilipokwisha kuiweka milango mahali pake, na mabawabu, waimbaji na Walawi walipokwisha kupewa kazi zao,
sw.R: Sasa ukuta ulikuwa umejengwa upya, nami nilikuwa nimetundika milango kwenye malango. Walinzi wa malango, waimbaji na Walawi walipewa kazi zao.

vi.L: Và xảy ra, khi tường thành đã được xây xong và tôi đã dựng các cánh cửa, và những người giữ cổng, những người ca hát và người Lê-vi đã được bổ nhiệm,
vi.B: Khi tường thành đã được xây lại và tôi đã lắp các cánh cửa vào chỗ, và những người giữ cổng, những người ca hát cùng người Lê-vi đã được giao nhiệm vụ,
vi.R: Bấy giờ tường thành đã được xây lại, và tôi đã lắp cánh cửa cho các cổng. Những người giữ cổng, những người ca hát và người Lê-vi được giao công việc của mình.

ko.L: 그리고 성벽이 다 세워지고 내가 문짝들을 달았으며, 문지기들과 노래하는 사람들과 레위 사람들이 임명되었을 때,
ko.B: 성벽이 다시 세워지고 내가 문짝들을 제자리에 달았으며, 문지기들과 노래하는 사람들과 레위 사람들이 각자 맡은 일에 임명되었을 때,
ko.R: 이제 성벽은 다시 세워졌고, 나는 성문마다 문짝을 달았다. 문지기들과 노래하는 사람들과 레위 사람들은 각자 맡을 일을 받았다.

pt.L: E aconteceu, quando o muro tinha sido construído e eu tinha colocado as portas, e os porteiros e os cantores e os levitas tinham sido designados,
pt.B: Quando o muro foi reconstruído e coloquei as portas no lugar, e os porteiros, os cantores e os levitas foram designados para as suas funções,
pt.R: O muro estava reconstruído, e eu tinha colocado as portas nas entradas da cidade. Os porteiros, os cantores e os levitas receberam as suas tarefas.

am.L: ቅጥሩም ከተሠራና መዝጊያዎቹን ካቆምኩ በኋላ፣ በር ጠባቂዎቹና መዘምራኑ ሌዋውያኑም ከተሾሙ በኋላ እንዲህ ሆነ፤
am.B: ቅጥሩ እንደ ገና ተሠርቶ መዝጊያዎቹን በየስፍራቸው ካቆምኩ በኋላ፣ በር ጠባቂዎቹ፣ መዘምራኑና ሌዋውያኑም በየሥራቸው ከተሾሙ በኋላ፣
am.R: ቅጥሩ አሁን እንደ ገና ተሠርቶ ነበር፤ እኔም በየበሩ መዝጊያዎቹን አቁሜ ነበር። በር ጠባቂዎቹ፣ መዘምራኑና ሌዋውያኑ የየሥራቸውን ተቀበሉ።

hi.L: और ऐसा हुआ कि जब शहरपनाह बन गई और मैंने किवाड़ लगा दिए, और द्वारपाल और गायक और लेवी नियुक्त किए गए,
hi.B: जब शहरपनाह फिर से बन गई और मैंने किवाड़ अपनी जगह लगा दिए, और द्वारपाल, गायक और लेवी अपने-अपने कामों पर नियुक्त कर दिए गए,
hi.R: शहरपनाह अब फिर से बन चुकी थी, और मैंने फाटकों में किवाड़ लगा दिए थे। द्वारपालों, गायकों और लेवियों को उनके काम सौंप दिए गए।

ru.L: И было, когда стена была отстроена и я поставил двери, и были назначены привратники, и певцы, и левиты,
ru.B: Когда стена была отстроена и я поставил на место двери, а привратники, певцы и левиты были назначены на свои обязанности,
ru.R: Стена была отстроена, и я навесил двери в воротах. Привратники, певцы и левиты получили свои обязанности.

ja.L: そして、城壁が建てられ、わたしが扉を取り付け、門衛たちと歌い手たちとレビ人たちが任命されたとき、
ja.B: 城壁が建て直され、わたしが扉を取り付け、門衛たちと歌い手たちとレビ人たちがそれぞれの務めに任命されたとき、
ja.R: 城壁はもう建て直され、わたしは門に扉を取り付けました。門番、歌い手、レビ人たちには、それぞれの仕事が与えられました。

uk.L: І сталося, коли стіну було збудовано і я поставив двері, і було призначено воротарів, і співаків, і левитів,
uk.B: Коли стіну відбудували, я навісив двері, і воротарів, співаків та левитів було призначено на їхні служби,
uk.R: Стіну вже відбудували, і я навісив двері в брамах. Воротарям, співакам і левитам доручили їхню роботу.

decisions.choice: the wall finished and the doors hung: the end of the building work of chapters 1-6
decisions.reason: The wall was completed in fifty-two days (6:15), and the gate doors, still missing in 6:1, are now set up. The memoir moves from building the wall to guarding and filling the city.

decisions.choice: were appointed: gatekeepers, singers and Levites given their posts
decisions.reason: The gatekeepers and singers belonged to the temple staff (verses 44-45). Here, with the city newly walled, gatekeepers are also needed at the city gates (verse 3), and the order in which the groups are named may reflect that.

decisions.choice: ends with a comma (Literal, Balanced); Readable makes two sentences
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence runs on into verse 2, where Nehemiah puts Hanani in charge. Literal and Balanced keep it open with a comma; Readable finishes the scene here and starts verse 2 afresh.

decisions.choice: Passé simple (Literal, Balanced), passé composé (Readable) for Nehemiah's memoir
decisions.reason: As in Ezra's memoir, Literal and Balanced tell the story in the passé simple (« je posai ») and Readable in the passé composé (« j'ai posé »), the tense of spoken French. Here the clause is anterior, so L and B use the passé antérieur (« j'eus dressé »).

decisions.choice: « les battants » for the doors (L); « les battants des portes » (B, R)
decisions.reason: French « portes » would also mean the gateways themselves; « battants » names the wooden doors hung in them, as in verse 3.

decisions.choice: "mabawabu" (L, B), "walinzi wa malango" (R)
decisions.reason: The gatekeepers are named as in Ezra 2:42 and 2:70.

decisions.choice: os porteiros, os cantores, os levitas
decisions.reason: The three groups of the temple staff (m2) keep the names Ezra 2 and Chronicles give them in Portuguese, so that the register of verses 44-45 names the same people. "Porteiros" are those who keep the gates, here also those of the city (verse 3).

decisions.choice: "ቅጥር" for the city wall (ḥomah) and "መዝጊያዎች" for the doors of the gates, through Nehemiah 7-9
decisions.reason: "ቅጥር" is the wall round a city; "ግንብ" is kept for the citadel (verse 2) and for towers. "መዝጊያ" is the door that closes a gateway.

decisions.choice: Literal ends with "እንዲህ ሆነ፤" ("it was so"), Balanced with a comma; verse 2 carries the main clause
decisions.reason: Amharic puts the time clauses ("... ከተሠራ በኋላ") first. Literal keeps the Hebrew "and it was" as a clause of its own; Balanced leaves the sentence open into verse 2, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "शहरपनाह", "किवाड़"; "द्वारपाल", "गायक"
decisions.reason: The wall and the doors keep the words of Nehemiah 3 and 6 (शहरपनाह, किवाड़ लगाना); the gatekeepers and singers keep the words of 1 Chronicles 9 and Ezra 2 (द्वारपाल, गायक).

decisions.choice: the sentence stays open with a comma (L, B) and runs on into verse 2; Readable makes two sentences
alternatives: a full stop at every level
decisions.reason: As in the English: the Hebrew sentence continues into verse 2, where Nehemiah puts Hanani in charge. "Привратники", "певцы", "левиты" as in Ezra and Nehemiah 10-13.

decisions.choice: sho'arim "門衛たち" (L, B), "門番" (R); meshorerim "歌い手たち"; L and B leave 7:1 open with "…とき、" into 7:2, as the English; R makes two sentences.
decisions.reason: The Chronicles and Ezra forms for the temple orders.

source.text: וָאֲצַוֶּ֞ה אֶת־חֲנָ֣נִי אָחִ֗י וְאֶת־חֲנַנְיָ֛ה שַׂ֥ר הַבִּירָ֖ה עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּי־הוּא֙ כְּאִ֣ישׁ אֱמֶ֔ת וְיָרֵ֥א אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים מֵרַבִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And I commanded Hanani my brother and Hananiah [the] commander of the citadel over Jerusalem, for he [was] like a man of faithfulness and fearing God more than many.

en.L: that I put Hanani my brother, and Hananiah the commander of the citadel, in charge over Jerusalem, for he [was] a faithful man and feared God more than many.
en.B: I put my brother Hanani in charge of Jerusalem, together with Hananiah the commander of the citadel, for he was a faithful man who feared God more than most.
en.R: I put my brother Hanani in charge of Jerusalem, along with Hananiah, the commander of the fortress. Hananiah was a man people could trust, and he respected God more than most people did.

es.L: que puse a Hananí mi hermano, y a Hananías el jefe de la ciudadela, al frente de Jerusalén, porque él [era] un hombre fiel y temía a Dios más que muchos.
es.B: puse a mi hermano Hananí al frente de Jerusalén, junto con Hananías, el jefe de la ciudadela, porque era un hombre fiel que temía a Dios más que la mayoría.
es.R: Puse a mi hermano Hananí al frente de Jerusalén, junto con Hananías, el comandante de la fortaleza. Hananías era un hombre de confianza, y respetaba a Dios más que la mayoría de la gente.

fr.L: que j’établis Hanani mon frère, et Hanania le chef de la citadelle, sur Jérusalem, car c’[était] un homme fidèle, et il craignait Dieu plus que beaucoup.
fr.B: j’établis mon frère Hanani à la tête de Jérusalem, avec Hanania, le chef de la citadelle, car c’était un homme fidèle qui craignait Dieu plus que la plupart.
fr.R: J’ai mis mon frère Hanani à la tête de Jérusalem, avec Hanania, le commandant de la forteresse. Hanania était un homme digne de confiance, et il respectait Dieu plus que la plupart des gens.

sw.L: kwamba nilimweka Hanani ndugu yangu, na Hanania mkuu wa ngome, juu ya Yerusalemu, kwa maana yeye [alikuwa] mtu mwaminifu, naye alimcha Mungu kuliko wengi.
sw.B: nilimweka ndugu yangu Hanani kuisimamia Yerusalemu, pamoja na Hanania mkuu wa ngome, kwa maana alikuwa mtu mwaminifu aliyemcha Mungu kuliko watu wengi.
sw.R: Nilimweka ndugu yangu Hanani kuisimamia Yerusalemu, pamoja na Hanania, mkuu wa ngome. Hanania alikuwa mtu wa kuaminika, naye alimheshimu Mungu kuliko watu wengi.

vi.L: thì tôi giao cho Ha-na-ni, người anh em của tôi, và Ha-na-nia, quan chỉ huy thành lũy, cai quản Giê-ru-sa-lem, vì ông [là] một người trung tín và kính sợ Đức Chúa Trời hơn nhiều người.
vi.B: tôi giao cho Ha-na-ni, người anh em của tôi, cai quản Giê-ru-sa-lem, cùng với Ha-na-nia, quan chỉ huy thành lũy, vì ông là người trung tín và kính sợ Đức Chúa Trời hơn phần đông người khác.
vi.R: Tôi giao cho Ha-na-ni, người anh em của tôi, cai quản Giê-ru-sa-lem, cùng với Ha-na-nia, người chỉ huy đồn lũy. Ha-na-nia là người đáng tin cậy, và ông tôn kính Đức Chúa Trời hơn phần đông người khác.

ko.L: 나는 내 형제 하나니와 성채의 지휘관 하나냐에게 예루살렘을 맡겼다. 그는 신실한 사람[이었고], 많은 사람보다 더 하나님을 경외했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 나는 내 형제 하나니에게 성채의 지휘관 하나냐와 함께 예루살렘을 맡겼다. 하나냐는 신실한 사람으로서 대부분의 사람보다 하나님을 더 경외했기 때문이다.
ko.R: 나는 내 형제 하나니에게 요새의 지휘관 하나냐와 함께 예루살렘을 맡겼다. 하나냐는 믿을 만한 사람이었고, 다른 사람들 대부분보다 하나님을 더 공경했다.

pt.L: que eu pus Hanani, meu irmão, e Hananias, o comandante da cidadela, no comando de Jerusalém, pois ele [era] um homem fiel e temia a Deus mais do que muitos.
pt.B: pus o meu irmão Hanani no comando de Jerusalém, junto com Hananias, o comandante da cidadela, pois ele era um homem fiel, que temia a Deus mais do que a maioria.
pt.R: Pus o meu irmão Hanani no comando de Jerusalém, junto com Hananias, o comandante da fortaleza. Hananias era um homem em quem as pessoas podiam confiar, e ele respeitava a Deus mais do que a maioria das pessoas.

am.L: ወንድሜን አናኒንና የግንቡን አለቃ ሐናንያን በኢየሩሳሌም ላይ ሾምኳቸው፤ እርሱ እንደ ታማኝ ሰው ነበረና፤ ከብዙዎችም ይልቅ እግዚአብሔርን ይፈራ ነበር።
am.B: ወንድሜን አናኒን ከግንቡ አለቃ ከሐናንያ ጋር በኢየሩሳሌም ላይ ሾምኳቸው፤ ሐናንያ ታማኝ ሰው ነበረና፤ ከብዙዎችም ይልቅ እግዚአብሔርን ይፈራ ነበር።
am.R: ወንድሜን አናኒን የምሽጉ አለቃ ከሆነው ከሐናንያ ጋር የኢየሩሳሌም ኃላፊዎች አደረግኳቸው። ሐናንያ ሰዎች የሚተማመኑበት ሰው ነበር፤ ከብዙ ሰዎችም ይልቅ እግዚአብሔርን ያከብር ነበር።

hi.L: कि मैंने अपने भाई हनानी को, और गढ़ के सरदार हनन्याह को, यरूशलेम पर अधिकार सौंपा, क्योंकि वह विश्वासयोग्य पुरुष [था] और बहुतों से बढ़कर परमेश्वर का भय मानता था।
hi.B: मैंने अपने भाई हनानी को, गढ़ के सरदार हनन्याह के साथ, यरूशलेम का अधिकारी ठहराया, क्योंकि वह विश्वासयोग्य पुरुष था और अधिकतर लोगों से बढ़कर परमेश्वर का भय मानता था।
hi.R: मैंने अपने भाई हनानी को, और गढ़ के सेनापति हनन्याह को, यरूशलेम का अधिकारी ठहराया। हनन्याह ऐसा व्यक्ति था जिस पर लोग भरोसा कर सकते थे, और वह अधिकतर लोगों से बढ़कर परमेश्वर का आदर करता था।

ru.L: я поставил Ханани, моего брата, и Хананию, начальника крепости, над Иерусалимом, потому что он [был] человеком верным и боялся Бога больше многих.
ru.B: я поставил моего брата Ханани над Иерусалимом вместе с Хананией, начальником крепости, потому что он был верным человеком и боялся Бога больше, чем многие.
ru.R: Я поставил моего брата Ханани управлять Иерусалимом вместе с Хананией, начальником крепости. Ханания был человеком, на которого можно положиться, и он чтил Бога больше, чем многие другие.

ja.L: わたしは、わたしの兄弟ハナニと、城塞の長ハナンヤに、エルサレムを任せた。彼は誠実な人であり、多くの人にまさって神を畏れていたからである。
ja.B: わたしは、兄弟ハナニと城塞の長ハナンヤに、エルサレムの管理を任せた。ハナンヤは誠実な人で、ほかの多くの人にまさって神を畏れていたからである。
ja.R: わたしは、兄弟のハナニに、とりでの隊長ハナンヤと一緒に、エルサレムの管理を任せました。ハナンヤは信頼できる人で、ほかのだれよりも神を敬っていました。

uk.L: то я поставив над Єрусалимом Ханані, мого брата, і Хананію, начальника фортеці, бо він [був] як чоловік вірний і боявся Бога більше, ніж багато [інших].
uk.B: я поставив над Єрусалимом свого брата Ханані разом з Хананією, начальником фортеці, бо той був вірною людиною і боявся Бога більше, ніж більшість.
uk.R: Я поставив над Єрусалимом свого брата Ханані разом з Хананією, начальником фортеці. Хананія був людиною, якій можна було довіряти, і він шанував Бога більше, ніж більшість людей.

decisions.choice: Hanani my brother: the brother who brought Nehemiah the news from Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Hanani came to Susa with others from Judah and told Nehemiah about the broken wall (1:2-3). The word for brother can also mean a relative, but 1:2 suggests a brother by birth.

decisions.choice: commander of the citadel: the officer over the fortress beside the temple
alternatives: one man: Hanani, that is, Hananiah
decisions.reason: The citadel was the fortress north of the temple whose gates needed timber in 2:8. Its commander held a military post. Some readers take the verse to name one man (Hanani, that is, Hananiah), but the Hebrew joins two names with "and", and verse 3 speaks to more than one person ("to them").

decisions.choice: like a man of faithfulness: a truly trustworthy man; feared God: honored God with reverence and obedience
decisions.reason: The "like" does not weaken the phrase; it marks him as the very picture of a reliable man. To fear God is to live in awe and obedience before him (Genesis 22:12; Nehemiah 5:15). "More than many" means he stood out among the people of his time.

decisions.choice: feared God (Literal, Balanced); respected God (Readable)
decisions.reason: For young readers "feared" suggests being afraid. Readable says "respected God" to give the sense of reverent honor; the meaning decision explains the word.

decisions.choice: "la ciudadela" (L, B), "la fortaleza" (R)
decisions.reason: The citadel beside the temple (2:8) is "ciudadela" at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "fortaleza", the plainer word, as the English says "fortress".

decisions.choice: « la citadelle » (L, B), « la forteresse » (R)
decisions.reason: As in Kings, « citadelle » for the fortified building; Readable uses the plainer « forteresse », as the English Readable says "fortress".

decisions.choice: "ngome" for the citadel at every level
decisions.reason: "Ngome" is the word used for the fortress at Ecbatana (Ezra 6:2) and for the royal citadel in Kings; it serves every level.

decisions.choice: Ha-na-ni, người anh em của tôi
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say whether Hanani was older or younger, so the neutral "người anh em" is used rather than "anh" or "em".

decisions.choice: "성채" (L, B), "요새" (R)
decisions.reason: "성채" as for the fortress at Ecbatana (Ezra 6:2); Readable says "요새", as the English Readable says "fortress".

decisions.choice: o comandante da cidadela (L, B); o comandante da fortaleza (R)
decisions.reason: "Cidadela" is the word 2:8 uses at Literal for the fortress beside the temple (m2); Balanced keeps it here, as the English Balanced keeps "citadel", and "comandante" says that the post was military. Readable says "fortaleza", as 2:8 does and as the English Readable says "fortress".

decisions.choice: "አናኒ" (Hanani, as the terms list), "ሐናንያ" (Hananiah, as 2 Chronicles 26:11); the citadel "ግንብ" (Literal, Balanced), "ምሽግ" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The citadel (birah) is the fortress beside the temple; Readable says "fortress" as the English does. "እግዚአብሔር" for ha-Elohim: the one God is meant and no YHWH stands beside it.

decisions.choice: Literal starts a new sentence with "ሾምኳቸው" (I put them in charge); the English Literal joins it to verse 1 with "that"
decisions.reason: Amharic cannot hang a "that"-clause on verse 1's "it was"; verse 1 closes with "እንዲህ ሆነ" and this verse states what happened.

decisions.choice: a man people could trust
decisions.reason: "A man of truth" is a man who can be relied on; Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: "हनानी", "हनन्याह"; "गढ़ का सरदार" (L, B), "गढ़ का सेनापति" (R)
decisions.reason: Hanani and Hananiah keep the forms of Nehemiah 1:2 and 3:30; the citadel is गढ़, as in Nehemiah 2:8. The commander (sar) of the citadel is सरदार, a military title kept apart from the civil leaders (हाकिम, अगुवे) of Nehemiah 3; Readable says सेनापति, since he commanded the fortress.

decisions.choice: "परमेश्वर का भय मानता था" (L, B); "परमेश्वर का आदर करता था" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English, Readable says that he honored God rather than that he was afraid; the meaning decision explains the fear of God.

decisions.choice: "Ханани", "Ханания", "крепость" (the citadel)
decisions.reason: The forms of Nehemiah 1:2 (Hanani), 3:8 and 10:24 (Hananiah) and 2:8 ("крепость" for the birah by the temple) in this translation.

decisions.choice: "боялся Бога" (L, B); "чтил Бога" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the English Readable, and as Nehemiah 5:15 in this translation: "чтил" gives reverent honour, not fright; the meaning decision explains the word.

decisions.choice: sar habbirah "城塞の長" (L, B), "とりでの隊長" (R), the fortress of 2:8.
decisions.reason: One form for the temple fortress through the book.

decisions.choice: "боявся Бога" (L, B), "шанував Бога" (R)
decisions.reason: The fear of God here is reverence and obedience; Readable says so plainly, as the English does with "respected".

source.text: וָאֹמַ֣ר לָהֶ֗ם לֹ֣א יִפָּֽתְח֞וּ שַׁעֲרֵ֤י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ עַד־חֹ֣ם הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ וְעַ֨ד הֵ֥ם עֹמְדִ֛ים יָגִ֥יפוּ הַדְּלָת֖וֹת וֶאֱחֹ֑זוּ וְהַעֲמֵ֗יד מִשְׁמְרוֹת֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם אִ֚ישׁ בְּמִשְׁמָר֔וֹ וְאִ֖ישׁ נֶ֥גֶד בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I said to them, Not shall be opened [the] gates of Jerusalem until [the] heat of the sun; and while they [are] standing, let them shut the doors and bar [them]; and appoint guards of [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem, each at his guard post and each in front of his house.

en.L: And I said to them, "The gates of Jerusalem shall not be opened until the sun is hot; and while they [are still] standing [on duty], let them shut the doors and bar [them]. And appoint guards from the inhabitants of Jerusalem, each at his post and each in front of his [own] house."
en.B: I said to them, "The gates of Jerusalem must not be opened until the sun is hot, and while the gatekeepers are still on duty, have them shut the doors and bar them. Appoint guards from the people who live in Jerusalem, some at their posts and some in front of their own houses."
en.R: I told them, "Do not open the gates of Jerusalem until the sun is high and hot. Have the doors shut and barred while the gatekeepers are still standing guard. Choose some of the people who live in Jerusalem to be guards. Put some at the guard posts and others in front of their own homes."

es.L: Y les dije: «No se abrirán las puertas de Jerusalén hasta que caliente el sol; y mientras ellos [aún] estén de pie [en su puesto], que cierren las hojas y [las] atranquen. Y {{plural_you:pongan|poned}} guardias de los habitantes de Jerusalén, cada uno en su puesto de guardia y cada uno frente a su [propia] casa».
es.B: Les dije: «Las puertas de Jerusalén no deben abrirse hasta que caliente el sol, y mientras los porteros todavía estén de servicio, {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} que cierren las hojas y las atranquen. {{plural_you:Pongan|Poned}} guardias de entre los que viven en Jerusalén, unos en sus puestos y otros frente a sus propias casas».
es.R: Les dije: «No {{plural_you:abran|abráis}} las puertas de Jerusalén hasta que el sol esté alto y caliente. {{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} cerrar y atrancar las puertas mientras los porteros todavía estén montando guardia. {{plural_you:Escojan|Escoged}} a algunos de los que viven en Jerusalén para que sean guardias. {{plural_you:Pongan|Poned}} a unos en los puestos de guardia y a otros frente a sus propias casas».

fr.L: Et je leur dis : « Les portes de Jérusalem ne seront pas ouvertes avant que le soleil soit chaud ; et pendant qu’ils [sont encore] debout [à leur poste], qu’on ferme les battants et qu’on [les] verrouille. Et établissez des gardes parmi les habitants de Jérusalem, chacun à son poste et chacun devant sa [propre] maison. »
fr.B: Je leur dis : « Les portes de Jérusalem ne doivent pas être ouvertes avant que le soleil soit chaud, et pendant que les portiers sont encore en service, faites fermer et verrouiller les battants. Établissez des gardes parmi les habitants de Jérusalem, les uns à leur poste, les autres devant leur propre maison. »
fr.R: Je leur ai dit : « N’ouvrez pas les portes de Jérusalem avant que le soleil soit haut et chaud. Faites fermer et verrouiller les portes pendant que les portiers montent encore la garde. Choisissez des gardes parmi les gens qui habitent à Jérusalem. Placez-en certains aux postes de garde et d’autres devant leur propre maison. »

sw.L: Nami nikawaambia, "Malango ya Yerusalemu yasifunguliwe mpaka jua liwe kali; na wakati wao [wangali] wamesimama [kazini], wafunge milango na kuweka makomeo. Tena wekeni walinzi kutoka kwa wakazi wa Yerusalemu, kila mmoja mahali pake pa ulinzi na kila mmoja mbele ya nyumba yake [mwenyewe]."
sw.B: Nikawaambia, "Malango ya Yerusalemu yasifunguliwe mpaka jua liwe kali, na wakati mabawabu wangali kazini, waagizeni wafunge milango na kuweka makomeo. Wekeni walinzi kutoka kwa watu wanaoishi Yerusalemu, wengine katika vituo vyao na wengine mbele ya nyumba zao wenyewe."
sw.R: Niliwaambia, "Msiyafungue malango ya Yerusalemu mpaka jua liwe juu na kuwaka. Milango ifungwe na kuwekewa makomeo wakati walinzi wa malango wangali wanalinda. Chagueni baadhi ya watu wanaoishi Yerusalemu wawe walinzi. Wekeni wengine kwenye vituo vya ulinzi na wengine mbele ya nyumba zao wenyewe."

vi.L: Và tôi nói với họ: "Các cổng thành Giê-ru-sa-lem sẽ không được mở cho đến khi mặt trời nóng; và trong khi họ [vẫn còn] đứng [canh], hãy cho họ đóng các cánh cửa lại và cài then [lại]. Và hãy lập những người canh gác từ dân cư Giê-ru-sa-lem, mỗi người tại vọng gác của mình và mỗi người trước nhà [riêng] của mình."
vi.B: Tôi bảo họ: "Không được mở các cổng thành Giê-ru-sa-lem cho đến khi mặt trời đã nóng, và trong khi những người giữ cổng còn đang canh, hãy bảo họ đóng các cánh cửa và cài then. Hãy cắt đặt người canh gác trong số dân sống tại Giê-ru-sa-lem, người thì ở vọng gác, người thì ở trước nhà mình."
vi.R: Tôi dặn họ: "Đừng mở các cổng thành Giê-ru-sa-lem cho đến khi mặt trời đã lên cao và nóng. Hãy cho đóng cửa và cài then trong khi những người giữ cổng vẫn còn đứng gác. Hãy chọn một số người sống tại Giê-ru-sa-lem làm người canh gác. Hãy đặt một số người ở các vọng gác, và những người khác ở trước nhà mình."

ko.L: 그리고 내가 그들에게 말했다. "해가 뜨거워질 때까지 예루살렘 성문들을 열어서는 안 되오. 그리고 그들이 [아직] 서 있는 [동안에] 문짝들을 닫고 빗장을 지르게 하시오. 또 예루살렘 주민들 가운데서 파수꾼들을 세우되, 각자 자기 초소에, 각자 자기 집 앞에 [세우시오]."
ko.B: 나는 그들에게 말했다. "해가 뜨거워지기 전에는 예루살렘 성문들을 열어서는 안 되오. 문지기들이 아직 지키고 있는 동안에 문을 닫고 빗장을 지르게 하시오. 예루살렘에 사는 사람들 가운데서 파수꾼들을 세워, 더러는 초소를 지키고 더러는 자기 집 앞을 지키게 하시오."
ko.R: 나는 그들에게 일렀다. "해가 높이 떠서 뜨거워지기 전에는 예루살렘 성문들을 열지 마시오. 문지기들이 아직 서서 지키고 있을 때 문을 닫고 빗장을 지르게 하시오. 예루살렘에 사는 사람들 가운데 몇 사람을 골라 파수꾼으로 세우시오. 더러는 초소에, 더러는 자기 집 앞에 세우시오."

pt.L: E eu lhes disse: "Não se abram as portas de Jerusalém até que o sol esteja quente; e, enquanto eles [ainda] estiverem de pé [no seu posto], fechem as portas e [as] tranquem. E designem guardas dentre os moradores de Jerusalém, cada um no seu posto e cada um diante da sua [própria] casa."
pt.B: Eu lhes disse: "As portas de Jerusalém não devem ser abertas antes que o sol esteja quente, e, enquanto os porteiros ainda estiverem de serviço, mandem fechar e trancar as portas. Designem guardas dentre os moradores de Jerusalém, uns nos seus postos e outros diante das suas próprias casas."
pt.R: Eu disse a eles: "Não abram as portas de Jerusalém até que o sol esteja alto e quente. Mandem fechar e trancar as portas enquanto os porteiros ainda estiverem montando guarda. Escolham algumas das pessoas que moram em Jerusalém para serem guardas. Ponham algumas nos postos de guarda e outras diante das suas próprias casas."

am.L: እንዲህም አልኳቸው፦ «ፀሐይ እስኪሞቅ ድረስ የኢየሩሳሌም በሮች አይከፈቱ፤ [በር ጠባቂዎቹም ገና] ቆመው ሳሉ መዝጊያዎቹን ይዝጉ፤ ይቀርቅሩም። ከኢየሩሳሌምም ነዋሪዎች ጠባቂዎችን አቁሙ፤ እያንዳንዱ በየጥበቃው ስፍራ፣ እያንዳንዱም በቤቱ ፊት [ይቁም]።»
am.B: እንዲህም አልኳቸው፦ «ፀሐይ እስኪሞቅ ድረስ የኢየሩሳሌም በሮች መከፈት የለባቸውም፤ በር ጠባቂዎቹም ገና በሥራቸው ላይ ሳሉ መዝጊያዎቹን አዘግተው ያስቀርቅሩ። በኢየሩሳሌም ከሚኖሩ ሰዎች ጠባቂዎችን ሹሙ፤ አንዳንዶቹ በየጥበቃ ስፍራቸው፣ አንዳንዶቹም በየቤታቸው ፊት ይቁሙ።»
am.R: እንዲህም አልኳቸው፦ «ፀሐይ ከፍ ብላ እስክትሞቅ ድረስ የኢየሩሳሌምን በሮች አትክፈቱ። በር ጠባቂዎቹ ገና ቆመው እየጠበቁ ሳሉ መዝጊያዎቹ ተዘግተው ይቀርቀሩ። በኢየሩሳሌም ከሚኖሩት ሰዎች አንዳንዶቹን ጠባቂዎች እንዲሆኑ ምረጡ። አንዳንዶቹን በጥበቃ ስፍራዎቹ፣ ሌሎቹንም በየቤታቸው ፊት አቁሙ።»

hi.L: और मैंने उनसे कहा, "जब तक धूप तेज़ न हो, तब तक यरूशलेम के फाटक न खोले जाएँ; और जब वे [अभी पहरे पर] खड़े हों, तभी वे किवाड़ बंद करें और [उन पर] बेंड़े लगाएँ। और यरूशलेम के निवासियों में से पहरेदार ठहराओ, हर एक को अपने पहरे पर और हर एक को अपने [ही] घर के सामने।"
hi.B: मैंने उनसे कहा, "जब तक धूप तेज़ न हो जाए, तब तक यरूशलेम के फाटक न खोले जाएँ, और जब द्वारपाल अभी पहरे पर ही हों, तभी उनसे किवाड़ बंद करवाकर उन पर बेंड़े लगवाओ। यरूशलेम में रहनेवाले लोगों में से पहरेदार ठहराओ, कुछ को उनकी चौकियों पर और कुछ को उनके अपने घरों के सामने।"
hi.R: मैंने उनसे कहा, "जब तक सूरज ऊपर चढ़कर तेज़ न हो जाए, तब तक यरूशलेम के फाटक मत खोलना। जब द्वारपाल अभी पहरे पर खड़े हों, तभी किवाड़ बंद करवाकर उन पर बेंड़े लगवा देना। यरूशलेम में रहनेवाले कुछ लोगों को पहरेदार चुनो। कुछ को पहरे की चौकियों पर रखो और कुछ को उनके अपने घरों के सामने।"

ru.L: И сказал я им: «Пусть не открываются ворота Иерусалима, пока не начнёт припекать солнце; и пока они [ещё] стоят [на страже], пусть закрывают двери и запирают [их]. И поставьте стражей из жителей Иерусалима, каждого на его посту и каждого напротив его [собственного] дома.»
ru.B: Я сказал им: «Ворота Иерусалима нельзя открывать, пока солнце не начнёт припекать, и пока привратники ещё на страже, пусть они закрывают двери и запирают их. Поставьте стражей из жителей Иерусалима: одних на их постах, других напротив их собственных домов.»
ru.R: Я сказал им: «Не открывайте ворота Иерусалима, пока солнце не поднимется высоко и не станет жарко. Пусть двери закрывают и запирают, пока привратники ещё стоят на страже. Выберите из жителей Иерусалима людей, которые будут стражами. Одних поставьте на сторожевые посты, а других — перед их собственными домами.»

ja.L: わたしは彼らに言った。「日が熱くなるまで、エルサレムの門を開いてはならない。彼らが[まだ番に]立っている間に、扉を閉じ、かんぬきを掛けさせよ。また、エルサレムの住民の中から見張りを立て、おのおのを自分の持ち場に、おのおのを自分の家の前に[置け]。」
ja.B: わたしは彼らに言った。「日が高く昇って暑くなるまで、エルサレムの門を開いてはならない。門衛たちがまだ番をしている間に、扉を閉じさせ、かんぬきを掛けさせよ。また、エルサレムの住民の中から見張りを立て、ある者は持ち場に、ある者は自分の家の前に置け。」
ja.R: わたしは彼らに言いました。「日が高く昇って暑くなるまで、エルサレムの門を開けてはいけない。門番たちがまだ見張りに立っている間に、扉を閉めて、かんぬきを掛けさせなさい。エルサレムに住む人々の中から、見張りをする人を選びなさい。ある人たちは見張りの場所に、ほかの人たちは自分の家の前に立たせなさい。」

uk.L: І я сказав їм: «Хай не відчиняють брам Єрусалима, доки не пригріє сонце; і поки вони [ще] стоять [на варті], хай зачиняють двері й замикають [їх]. І поставте варту з мешканців Єрусалима, кожного на його посту і кожного навпроти його [власного] дому.»
uk.B: Я сказав їм: «Брами Єрусалима не можна відчиняти, доки не пригріє сонце, а поки воротарі ще на варті, хай зачиняють двері й замикають їх. Поставте варту з мешканців Єрусалима: одних на їхніх постах, а інших навпроти їхніх власних домів.»
uk.R: Я наказав їм: «Не відчиняйте брам Єрусалима, доки сонце не підніметься високо й не пригріє. Хай двері зачиняють і замикають, поки воротарі ще стоять на варті. Виберіть з мешканців Єрусалима людей, щоб вони були вартовими. Одних поставте на сторожових постах, а інших — навпроти їхніх власних домів.»

decisions.choice: I said: the reading of the margin, not the written "he said"
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text can be read "and he said"; the scribes' note in the margin reads "and I said". The marginal reading fits the first-person memoir, where Nehemiah gives the orders, and it is followed here.

decisions.choice: until the heat of the sun: not before the sun is well up and hot
alternatives: not during the heat of the day
decisions.reason: The gates stay shut until well into the morning, when many people are about and an enemy could not slip in unseen at dawn. The words can also be read as "during the heat of the sun": do not open the gates in the hot middle of the day, when the guards rest. The first reading fits the order to close and bar the gates while the guards are still on duty.

decisions.choice: while they are standing: while the gatekeepers are still at their posts
decisions.reason: "They" are most naturally the gatekeepers of verse 1. The gates are to be shut and barred while they are still on duty, not left for later. "Bar" translates a verb meaning "take hold, fasten".

decisions.choice: guards from the inhabitants: residents guarding their own part of the city
decisions.reason: As the builders each repaired the wall near their own houses (3:10, 23, 28-30), the residents now keep watch near their homes. With few people in the city (verse 4), every resident is needed.

decisions.choice: the gatekeepers are still on duty (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the gatekeepers and add "still on duty" so that "they are standing" is not read as standing outside the gate. Literal brackets "still" and "on duty".

decisions.choice: plural_you for Nehemiah's orders to Hanani and Hananiah
decisions.reason: Nehemiah speaks to the two men he has put in charge, so the commands are plural: "ustedes" forms by default, "vosotros" forms as the reader setting.

decisions.choice: Nehemiah gives his orders in 하오체 ("열지 마시오", "세우시오")
decisions.reason: As governor he speaks to officials he has appointed in 하오체, the form used for his words to the nobles and officials in this book.

decisions.choice: vocês (Nehemiah to Hanani and Hananiah)
decisions.reason: Nehemiah, the governor, gives orders to the two men he has just put in charge, so he says "vocês", as a superior speaks to those under him in the Old Testament in Portuguese; the commands are plural in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: Nehemiah speaks to Hanani and Hananiah, whom he has put in charge, with the plain plural "እናንተ" (አቁሙ, ሹሙ)
decisions.reason: Nehemiah is the governor giving orders to the men he has appointed; the honorific would reverse the relationship.

decisions.choice: "जब द्वारपाल अभी पहरे पर ही हों" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English, Balanced and Readable name the gatekeepers, so that "while they are standing" is read as their being on duty; Literal brackets the words it supplies. The doors are barred with बेंड़े, the word of Nehemiah 3:3.

decisions.choice: "пока привратники ещё на страже" (B), "пока привратники ещё стоят на страже" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the English, Balanced and Readable name the gatekeepers so that "they are standing" is not read as someone standing outside the gate; Literal brackets the supplied words.

decisions.choice: Nehemiah's orders to Hanani and Hananiah in the plain style: "〜てはならない…させよ" (L, B), "〜てはいけない…させなさい" (R).
decisions.reason: A governor's commands; the qere "I said" is followed, as the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: 'ad chom hashshemesh "日が熱くなるまで" (L), "日が高く昇って暑くなるまで" (B, R).
decisions.reason: The sense is uncertain (meaning decision); B and R follow the English "until the sun is hot" with what it implies.

source.text: וְהָעִ֞יר רַחֲבַ֤ת יָדַ֨יִם֙ וּגְדוֹלָ֔ה וְהָעָ֥ם מְעַ֖ט בְּתוֹכָ֑הּ וְאֵ֥ין בָּתִּ֖ים בְּנוּיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And the city [was] wide of hands and great, and the people [were] few in its midst, and there were no houses built.

en.L: And the city [was] wide on [both] sides and large, but the people in it [were] few, and no houses had been built.
en.B: The city was spacious and large, but there were few people in it, and the houses had not been rebuilt.
en.R: Jerusalem was large and spread out, but only a few people lived in it. The houses had not yet been rebuilt.

es.L: Y la ciudad [era] ancha de [ambos] lados y grande, pero el pueblo dentro de ella [era] poco, y no había casas edificadas.
es.B: La ciudad era espaciosa y grande, pero había poca gente en ella, y las casas no se habían reconstruido.
es.R: Jerusalén era grande y extensa, pero vivía muy poca gente allí. Las casas todavía no se habían reconstruido.

fr.L: Et la ville [était] large des [deux] côtés et grande, mais le peuple au milieu d’elle [était] peu nombreux, et il n’y avait pas de maisons bâties.
fr.B: La ville était vaste et grande, mais il y avait peu de gens à l’intérieur, et les maisons n’avaient pas été rebâties.
fr.R: Jérusalem était grande et étendue, mais très peu de gens y habitaient. Les maisons n’avaient pas encore été reconstruites.

sw.L: Na mji [ulikuwa] mpana pande [zote] na mkubwa, lakini watu ndani yake [walikuwa] wachache, wala hapakuwa na nyumba zilizojengwa.
sw.B: Mji ulikuwa mpana na mkubwa, lakini watu waliokuwa ndani yake walikuwa wachache, na nyumba zilikuwa hazijajengwa upya.
sw.R: Yerusalemu ulikuwa mji mkubwa na uliotanuka, lakini watu wachache tu ndio walioishi ndani yake. Nyumba zilikuwa bado hazijajengwa upya.

vi.L: Và thành [thì] rộng [cả hai] phía và lớn, nhưng dân trong thành [thì] ít, và không có nhà nào được xây.
vi.B: Thành thì rộng rãi và lớn, nhưng dân cư trong thành thì ít, và nhà cửa chưa được xây lại.
vi.R: Giê-ru-sa-lem là một thành lớn và rộng, nhưng chỉ có ít người sống trong đó. Nhà cửa vẫn chưa được xây lại.

ko.L: 그리고 그 성읍은 [양] 쪽으로 넓고 컸으나, 그 안에 백성은 적었고, 지어진 집들이 없었다.
ko.B: 성읍은 넓고 컸지만, 그 안에 사는 사람은 적었고 집들은 아직 다시 지어지지 않았다.
ko.R: 예루살렘은 크고 넓었지만, 그 안에 사는 사람은 얼마 되지 않았다. 집들도 아직 다시 짓지 못한 상태였다.

pt.L: E a cidade [era] larga de [ambos os] lados e grande, mas o povo nela [era] pouco, e não havia casas construídas.
pt.B: A cidade era espaçosa e grande, mas havia pouca gente nela, e as casas não tinham sido reconstruídas.
pt.R: Jerusalém era grande e espaçosa, mas só pouca gente morava nela. As casas ainda não tinham sido reconstruídas.

am.L: ከተማዪቱም በሁለቱም ወገን ሰፊና ታላቅ ነበረች፤ በውስጧ ያለው ሕዝብ ግን ጥቂት ነበረ፤ ቤቶችም አልተሠሩም ነበር።
am.B: ከተማዪቱ ሰፊና ታላቅ ነበረች፤ በውስጧ የሚኖሩት ሰዎች ግን ጥቂቶች ነበሩ፤ ቤቶቹም እንደ ገና አልተሠሩም ነበር።
am.R: ኢየሩሳሌም ትልቅና ሰፊ ከተማ ነበረች፤ በውስጧ የሚኖሩት ግን ጥቂት ሰዎች ብቻ ነበሩ። ቤቶቹ ገና እንደ ገና አልተሠሩም ነበር።

hi.L: और नगर [दोनों] ओर चौड़ा और बड़ा [था], पर उसमें लोग थोड़े [थे], और घर बने नहीं थे।
hi.B: नगर चौड़ा और बड़ा था, पर उसमें लोग थोड़े थे, और घर फिर से नहीं बनाए गए थे।
hi.R: यरूशलेम बड़ा था और दूर तक फैला हुआ था, पर उसमें थोड़े ही लोग रहते थे। घर अभी फिर से नहीं बनाए गए थे।

ru.L: А город [был] широк в [обе] стороны и велик, но народа в нём [было] мало, и дома не были построены.
ru.B: Город был просторным и большим, но людей в нём было мало, и дома ещё не были отстроены.
ru.R: Иерусалим был большим и просторным, но в нём жило мало людей. Дома ещё не были отстроены заново.

ja.L: 町は両側に広く、大きかったが、その中の民は少なく、家々は建てられていなかった。
ja.B: 町は広々として大きかったが、その中に住む民は少なく、家々もまだ建て直されていなかった。
ja.R: エルサレムは大きく広がっていましたが、そこに住んでいる人はわずかでした。家々も、まだ建て直されていませんでした。

uk.L: А місто [було] широке на [обидві] руки і велике, а народу в ньому [було] мало, і доми не були збудовані.
uk.B: Місто було просторе й велике, але людей у ньому було мало, і доми ще не були відбудовані.
uk.R: Єрусалим був великий і просторий, але жило в ньому лише кілька людей. Доми ще не були відбудовані.

decisions.choice: wide of hands: spacious, broad in every direction
decisions.reason: "Wide of hands" (or "of both sides") is a Hebrew way of saying a place stretches out on every side (Genesis 34:21; Psalm 104:25).

decisions.choice: no houses built: the city was not yet built up with homes
decisions.reason: Some houses stood (the builders worked beside their houses, 3:20-30), so the words do not mean that there was not a single house. The city was largely empty of homes and families. This leads to Nehemiah's plan to enroll the people (verse 5) and to bring one in ten to live in Jerusalem (11:1-2).

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן אֱלֹהַי֙ אֶל־לִבִּ֔י וָאֶקְבְּצָ֞ה אֶת־הַחֹרִ֧ים וְאֶת־הַסְּגָנִ֛ים וְאֶת־הָעָ֖ם לְהִתְיַחֵ֑שׂ וָֽאֶמְצָ֗א סֵ֤פֶר הַיַּ֨חַשׂ֙ הָעוֹלִ֣ים בָּרִאשׁוֹנָ֔ה וָאֶמְצָ֖א כָּת֥וּב בּֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And put my God into my heart, and I gathered the nobles and the officials and the people to be enrolled by genealogy; and I found [the] book of the genealogy of the ones coming up at the first, and I found written in it:

en.L: And my God put [it] into my heart, and I gathered the nobles and the officials and the people to be enrolled by genealogy. And I found the book of the genealogy of those who came up at the first, and I found written in it:
en.B: Then my God put it into my heart to gather the nobles, the officials and the people to be enrolled by their family lines. I found the genealogical record of those who had come back first, and this is what I found written in it:
en.R: Then my God gave me the idea to call together the leaders, the officials and the people, so that they could be listed by their families. I found the family record of those who had come back from exile first. This is what was written in it:

es.L: Y mi Dios puso [esto] en mi corazón, y reuní a los nobles y a los oficiales y al pueblo para que fueran inscritos por genealogía. Y encontré el libro de la genealogía de los que subieron al principio, y encontré escrito en él:
es.B: Entonces mi Dios puso en mi corazón reunir a los nobles, a los oficiales y al pueblo para que fueran inscritos según sus linajes. Encontré el registro genealógico de los que habían regresado primero, y esto es lo que encontré escrito en él:
es.R: Entonces mi Dios me dio la idea de reunir a los líderes, a los funcionarios y al pueblo, para que fueran registrados por familias. Encontré el registro de familias de los que habían regresado primero del destierro. Esto es lo que estaba escrito en él:

fr.L: Et mon Dieu [le] mit dans mon cœur, et je rassemblai les notables et les magistrats et le peuple pour qu’ils soient inscrits par généalogie. Et je trouvai le livre de la généalogie de ceux qui étaient montés au commencement, et je trouvai écrit dedans :
fr.B: Alors mon Dieu me mit au cœur de rassembler les notables, les magistrats et le peuple pour qu’ils soient inscrits selon leurs familles. Je trouvai le registre généalogique de ceux qui étaient revenus les premiers, et voici ce que j’y trouvai écrit :
fr.R: Alors mon Dieu m’a donné l’idée de réunir les chefs, les responsables et le peuple, pour qu’on les inscrive par familles. J’ai trouvé le registre des familles de ceux qui étaient revenus de l’exil les premiers. Voici ce qui y était écrit :

sw.L: Na Mungu wangu akatia [jambo hili] moyoni mwangu, nami nikawakusanya wakuu na maafisa na watu ili waandikwe kwa nasaba. Nami nikakiona kitabu cha nasaba ya wale waliopanda hapo kwanza, nami nikaona imeandikwa ndani yake:
sw.B: Kisha Mungu wangu akatia moyoni mwangu niwakusanye wakuu, maafisa na watu ili waandikwe kwa koo zao. Nikakiona kitabu cha orodha ya ukoo ya wale waliorudi kwanza, na hiki ndicho nilichokikuta kimeandikwa ndani yake:
sw.R: Kisha Mungu wangu akanipa wazo la kuwakusanya viongozi, maafisa na watu, ili waandikwe kwa jamaa zao. Nikaipata kumbukumbu ya jamaa za wale waliorudi kwanza kutoka uhamishoni. Hiki ndicho kilichokuwa kimeandikwa ndani yake:

vi.L: Và Đức Chúa Trời của tôi đặt [điều này] vào lòng tôi, và tôi nhóm họp các nhà quý tộc, các quan chức và dân chúng để được ghi vào gia phả. Và tôi tìm thấy sách gia phả của những người đã đi lên lúc ban đầu, và tôi thấy có chép trong đó:
vi.B: Bấy giờ Đức Chúa Trời của tôi đặt vào lòng tôi ý muốn nhóm họp các nhà quý tộc, các quan chức và dân chúng để ghi danh theo gia phả. Tôi tìm thấy sổ gia phả của những người đã trở về đầu tiên, và đây là điều tôi thấy chép trong đó:
vi.R: Bấy giờ Đức Chúa Trời của tôi cho tôi ý định triệu tập những người lãnh đạo, các quan chức và dân chúng để ghi tên họ theo từng gia đình. Tôi tìm thấy sổ ghi chép các gia đình của những người đầu tiên từ chốn lưu đày trở về. Trong đó có chép như sau:

ko.L: 그리고 내 하나님께서 내 마음에 [생각을] 넣어 주셔서, 나는 귀족들과 관리들과 백성을 모아 족보에 따라 등록하게 했다. 그리고 나는 처음에 올라온 사람들의 족보책을 찾았는데, 그 안에 이렇게 기록되어 있는 것을 발견했다.
ko.B: 그때 내 하나님께서 내 마음을 움직이셔서, 나는 귀족들과 관리들과 백성을 모아 집안별로 등록하게 했다. 나는 처음에 돌아온 사람들의 족보 기록을 찾았는데, 거기에 이렇게 쓰여 있었다.
ko.R: 그때 내 하나님께서 나에게 지도자들과 관리들과 백성을 불러 모아 집안별로 이름을 올리게 할 생각을 주셨다. 나는 포로 생활에서 맨 처음 돌아온 사람들의 집안 기록을 찾았다. 거기에 이렇게 쓰여 있었다.

pt.L: E o meu Deus pôs [isto] no meu coração, e reuni os nobres e os oficiais e o povo para serem registrados por genealogia. E achei o livro da genealogia dos que subiram no princípio, e achei escrito nele:
pt.B: Então o meu Deus pôs no meu coração reunir os nobres, os oficiais e o povo, para que fossem registrados segundo as suas famílias. Encontrei o registro genealógico dos que tinham voltado primeiro, e isto é o que encontrei escrito nele:
pt.R: Então o meu Deus me deu a ideia de reunir os líderes, os oficiais e o povo, para que fossem registrados por famílias. Encontrei o registro das famílias dos que tinham voltado do exílio primeiro. Isto é o que estava escrito nele:

am.L: አምላኬም በልቤ አኖረ፤ ታላላቆቹንና ሹማምንቱን ሕዝቡንም በትውልድ እንዲመዘገቡ ሰበሰብኳቸው። በመጀመሪያም የወጡትን ሰዎች የትውልድ መጽሐፍ አገኘሁ፤ በእርሱም ተጽፎ አገኘሁ፦
am.B: ከዚያም አምላኬ ታላላቆቹን፣ ሹማምንቱንና ሕዝቡን በየቤተሰባቸው እንዲመዘገቡ እንድሰበስብ በልቤ አሳሰበኝ። በመጀመሪያ የተመለሱትን ሰዎች የትውልድ መዝገብ አገኘሁ፤ በእርሱም ተጽፎ ያገኘሁት ይህ ነው፦
am.R: ከዚያም አምላኬ መሪዎቹን፣ ሹማምንቱንና ሕዝቡን በየቤተሰባቸው እንዲመዘገቡ እንድጠራቸው ሐሳብ ሰጠኝ። ከግዞት በመጀመሪያ የተመለሱትን ሰዎች የቤተሰብ መዝገብ አገኘሁ። በእርሱም የተጻፈው ይህ ነው፦

hi.L: और मेरे परमेश्वर ने मेरे मन में [यह] डाला, और मैंने कुलीनों और अधिकारियों और लोगों को इकट्ठा किया कि वंशावली के अनुसार उनके नाम लिखे जाएँ। और मुझे उन लोगों की वंशावली की पुस्तक मिली जो पहले ऊपर आए थे, और मैंने उसमें यह लिखा पाया:
hi.B: तब मेरे परमेश्वर ने मेरे मन में यह डाला कि मैं कुलीनों, अधिकारियों और लोगों को इकट्ठा करूँ, कि उनके परिवारों के अनुसार उनके नाम लिखे जाएँ। मुझे उन लोगों की वंशावली का लेखा मिला जो पहले लौटकर आए थे, और उसमें मैंने यह लिखा पाया:
hi.R: तब मेरे परमेश्वर ने मुझे यह विचार दिया कि मैं कुलीनों, अधिकारियों और लोगों को इकट्ठा करूँ, ताकि उनके परिवारों के अनुसार उनके नाम लिखे जा सकें। मुझे उन लोगों के परिवारों की सूची मिली जो सबसे पहले बंधुआई से लौटे थे। उसमें यह लिखा था:

ru.L: И вложил мой Бог в моё сердце, и я собрал знатных, и начальников, и народ, чтобы записать [их] по родословиям. И я нашёл книгу родословия тех, кто поднялся вначале, и нашёл в ней написанное:
ru.B: Тогда мой Бог вложил мне в сердце собрать знатных, начальников и народ, чтобы записать их по родам. Я нашёл родословный список тех, кто вернулся первыми, и вот что я нашёл в нём написанным:
ru.R: Тогда мой Бог дал мне мысль созвать знатных людей, начальников и народ, чтобы переписать всех по семьям. Я нашёл родословный список тех, кто первыми вернулся из изгнания. Вот что было в нём написано:

ja.L: わたしの神はわたしの心に[思いを]置かれ、わたしは貴族たちと役人たちと民を集めて、系図に登録させようとした。そして、わたしは最初に上って来た者たちの系図の書を見つけ、その中にこう書かれているのを見つけた。
ja.B: そのとき、わたしの神がわたしの心に思いを置かれたので、わたしは貴族たちと役人たちと民を集めて、家系ごとに登録させることにした。わたしは、最初に帰って来た者たちの系図の記録を見つけた。そこには、次のように書かれていた。
ja.R: そのとき、わたしの神は、わたしにある考えを与えてくださいました。それは、指導者たちと役人たちと人々を呼び集めて、家族ごとに名簿に載せることでした。わたしは、捕囚から最初に帰って来た人々の家族の記録を見つけました。そこには、次のように書かれていました。

uk.L: І мій Бог поклав мені на серце, і я зібрав знатних, і урядовців, і народ, щоб записати [їх] за родоводом. І я знайшов книгу родоводу тих, що піднялися спочатку, і знайшов написане в ній:
uk.B: Тоді мій Бог поклав мені на серце зібрати знатних, урядовців і народ, щоб записати їх за родоводами. Я знайшов родовідний запис тих, хто повернувся першим, і ось що знайшов у ньому написаним:
uk.R: Тоді мій Бог підказав мені скликати провідників, урядовців і народ, щоб записати всіх за родинами. Я знайшов родинний запис тих, хто першим повернувся з вигнання. Ось що в ньому було написано:

decisions.choice: my God put it into my heart: God gave me the purpose and the idea
decisions.reason: Nehemiah speaks of God's prompting as he did in 2:12. "Heart" in Hebrew is the seat of thinking and planning as well as feeling.

decisions.choice: nobles and officials: the leading families and the local officials
decisions.reason: The same pair appears in 2:16; 4:8, 13; 5:7. To be "enrolled by genealogy" is to be registered by family line, which settled who belonged to Israel and where each family had its rights.

decisions.choice: the book of the genealogy of those who came up at the first: the list of the earliest returnees
decisions.reason: The list that follows (verses 6-72) is the register of the first return from Babylon under Zerubbabel and Jeshua, some ninety years before Nehemiah. It appears also in Ezra 2:1-70 with small differences in names and numbers. Nehemiah uses it as the starting point for resettling Jerusalem (11:1-2).

decisions.choice: nobles and officials (Literal, Balanced); leaders and officials (Readable)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Ezra and Nehemiah, Readable uses "leaders" for the nobles, a plainer word for the heads of the leading families.

decisions.choice: os nobres e os oficiais (L, B); os líderes e os oficiais (R)
decisions.reason: The pair of 2:16 (m2): "nobres" for the leading families and "oficiais" for the local officials; Readable says "líderes", as the English Readable says "leaders". "Registrar por genealogia" and "o registro" keep the words Ezra 2:62 uses in Portuguese for the same register.

decisions.choice: nobles "ታላላቆች" (Literal, Balanced), "መሪዎች" (Readable); officials (seganim) "ሹማምንት", as Ezra on main
decisions.reason: The nobles are the leading families; Readable says "leaders" as the English. The officials are the local office-holders.

decisions.choice: "कुलीन"; "अधिकारी"
decisions.reason: The nobles and officials keep the words of Nehemiah 2:16 and 5:7: the nobles are कुलीन and the officials अधिकारी at every level.

decisions.choice: "знатные" (L, B), "знатные люди" (R); "начальники"
decisions.reason: The pair settled for Nehemiah at 2:16 in this translation: the nobles are "знатные", the officials "начальники".

decisions.choice: hityachses "系図に登録させる" (L), "家系ごとに登録させる" (B), "家族ごとに名簿に載せる" (R); sefer hayyachas "系図の書" (L), "系図の記録" (B), "家族の記録" (R).
decisions.reason: As 2 Chronicles 31:16-19; the register that follows (7:6-72) repeats Ezra 2.

source.text: אֵ֣לֶּה׀בְּנֵ֣י הַמְּדִינָ֗ה הָעֹלִים֙ מִשְּׁבִ֣י הַגּוֹלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶגְלָ֔ה נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֖ר מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֑ל וַיָּשׁ֧וּבוּ לִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם וְלִיהוּדָ֖ה אִ֥ישׁ לְעִירֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: These [are the] sons of the province, the ones coming up from the captivity of the exile whom had exiled Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and they returned to Jerusalem and to Judah, each to his city,

en.L: These [are] the sons of the province who came up from the captivity of the exiles, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried into exile, and they returned to Jerusalem and to Judah, each to his [own] city,
en.B: These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity of the exiles whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away, and who returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to their own town.
en.R: These are the people of the province of Judah who came back from exile. King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon had taken them away as captives. Now they returned to Jerusalem and to the rest of Judah, each to their own town.

es.L: Estos [son] los hijos de la provincia que subieron del cautiverio del destierro, a quienes Nabucodonosor rey de Babilonia había llevado al destierro, y volvieron a Jerusalén y a Judá, cada uno a su [propia] ciudad,
es.B: Estos son los de la provincia que subieron del cautiverio de los desterrados, a quienes Nabucodonosor rey de Babilonia había deportado, y que volvieron a Jerusalén y a Judá, cada uno a su propia ciudad.
es.R: Estos son los de la provincia de Judá que regresaron del destierro. Nabucodonosor, rey de Babilonia, se los había llevado presos. Ahora volvieron a Jerusalén y al resto de Judá, cada uno a su propia ciudad.

fr.L: Voici les fils de la province qui montèrent de la captivité de l’exil, que Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, avait déportés, et ils revinrent à Jérusalem et en Juda, chacun dans sa [propre] ville,
fr.B: Voici les gens de la province qui remontèrent de la captivité des exilés que Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, avait déportés, et qui revinrent à Jérusalem et en Juda, chacun dans sa ville.
fr.R: Voici les gens de la province de Juda qui sont revenus de l’exil. Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, les avait emmenés comme prisonniers. Ils sont alors revenus à Jérusalem et dans le reste de Juda, chacun dans sa propre ville.

sw.L: Hawa [ndio] wana wa jimbo waliopanda kutoka katika utumwa wa uhamisho, ambao Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli alikuwa amewahamisha, nao wakarudi Yerusalemu na Yuda, kila mmoja kwenye mji wake [mwenyewe],
sw.B: Hawa ndio watu wa jimbo waliopanda kutoka katika utumwa wa uhamisho, ambao Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli alikuwa amewachukua mateka, nao wakarudi Yerusalemu na Yuda, kila mmoja kwenye mji wake.
sw.R: Hawa ndio watu wa jimbo la Yuda waliorudi kutoka uhamishoni. Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli alikuwa amewachukua kama wafungwa. Sasa walirudi Yerusalemu na sehemu nyingine za Yuda, kila mmoja kwenye mji wake.

vi.L: Đây [là] các con của tỉnh [Giu-đa] đã đi lên từ cảnh phu tù của những người lưu đày, là những người Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn đã bắt lưu đày, và họ trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem và về Giu-đa, mỗi người về thành [của] mình,
vi.B: Đây là những người thuộc tỉnh Giu-đa đã ra khỏi cảnh phu tù mà trở lên, tức những người lưu đày mà Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn đã bắt đem đi, và họ đã trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem và Giu-đa, ai nấy về thành của mình.
vi.R: Đây là những người thuộc tỉnh Giu-đa đã từ chốn lưu đày trở về. Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn đã bắt họ làm tù binh, đem đi. Nay họ trở về Giê-ru-sa-lem và các nơi khác trong Giu-đa, ai nấy về thành của mình.

ko.L: 이들은 그 지방의 자손들이다. 그들은 바빌론 왕 느부갓네살이 사로잡아 갔던 포로들 가운데서 올라와, 예루살렘과 유다로, 각자 자기 성읍으로 돌아왔다.
ko.B: 이들은 바빌론 왕 느부갓네살이 사로잡아 갔던 포로들 가운데서 올라온 그 지방 사람들이다. 그들은 예루살렘과 유다로, 각자 자기 성읍으로 돌아왔다.
ko.R: 이들은 포로 생활에서 돌아온 유다 지방 사람들이다. 바빌론 왕 느부갓네살이 그들을 포로로 잡아갔었다. 이제 그들은 예루살렘과 유다의 다른 곳으로, 각자 자기 성읍으로 돌아왔다.

pt.L: Estes [são] os filhos da província que subiram do cativeiro do exílio, os que Nabucodonosor, rei da Babilônia, tinha levado ao exílio, e voltaram para Jerusalém e para Judá, cada um para a sua cidade,
pt.B: Este é o povo da província que voltou do cativeiro dos exilados que Nabucodonosor, rei da Babilônia, tinha deportado, e que voltou para Jerusalém e Judá, cada um para a sua cidade.
pt.R: Esta é a lista das pessoas da província de Judá que voltaram do exílio. Nabucodonosor, rei da Babilônia, as tinha levado como prisioneiras. Agora elas voltaram para Jerusalém e para o resto de Judá. Cada família voltou para a sua própria cidade.

am.L: የባቢሎን ንጉሥ ናቡከደነፆር ካፈለሳቸው ምርኮኞች ግዞት የወጡት የአውራጃው ልጆች እነዚህ ናቸው፤ እነርሱም ወደ ኢየሩሳሌምና ወደ ይሁዳ፣ እያንዳንዱ ወደ ከተማው ተመለሱ፤
am.B: የባቢሎን ንጉሥ ናቡከደነፆር አፍልሶ ከወሰዳቸው ምርኮኞች መካከል ከግዞት የወጡት የአውራጃው ሰዎች እነዚህ ናቸው። እነርሱም ወደ ኢየሩሳሌምና ወደ ይሁዳ፣ እያንዳንዳቸው ወደ ገዛ ከተማቸው ተመለሱ።
am.R: ከግዞት የተመለሱት የይሁዳ አውራጃ ሰዎች እነዚህ ናቸው። የባቢሎን ንጉሥ ናቡከደነፆር በምርኮ ወስዷቸው ነበር። አሁን ወደ ኢየሩሳሌምና ወደ ሌሎቹ የይሁዳ ከተሞች፣ እያንዳንዳቸው ወደ ገዛ ከተማቸው ተመለሱ።

hi.L: ये उस प्रांत के पुत्र [हैं] जो निर्वासितों की बंधुआई से ऊपर आए, जिन्हें बाबुल का राजा नबूकदनेस्सर बंधुआई में ले गया था, और वे यरूशलेम को और यहूदा को, हर एक अपने नगर को, लौट आए,
hi.B: ये उस प्रांत के लोग हैं जो उन निर्वासितों की बंधुआई से निकलकर आए जिन्हें बाबुल का राजा नबूकदनेस्सर ले गया था, और जो यरूशलेम और यहूदा को, हर एक अपने-अपने नगर को, लौट आए।
hi.R: यह यहूदा प्रांत के उन लोगों की सूची है जो बंधुआई से लौटे। बाबुल का राजा नबूकदनेस्सर उन्हें बंदी बनाकर ले गया था। अब वे यरूशलेम और यहूदा के बाक़ी भागों में लौट आए। हर परिवार अपने-अपने नगर को लौटा।

ru.L: Вот сыновья области, которые поднялись из плена изгнания, которых переселил Навуходоносор, царь Вавилона, и они возвратились в Иерусалим и в Иуду, каждый в свой город,
ru.B: Вот жители области, вернувшиеся из плена, — изгнанники, которых угнал Навуходоносор, царь Вавилона. Они возвратились в Иерусалим и в Иуду, каждый в свой город,
ru.R: Вот список жителей области Иуды, которые вернулись из изгнания. Навуходоносор, царь Вавилона, увёл их в плен. Теперь они вернулись в Иерусалим и в остальную Иуду. Каждая семья вернулась в свой город.

ja.L: これらは州の子らで、捕囚の民の捕らわれの身から上って来た者たち、すなわちバビロンの王ネブカドネツァルが捕らえ移していた者たちであり、エルサレムとユダへ、それぞれ自分の町へ帰った者たちで、
ja.B: これは、バビロンの王ネブカドネツァルが捕らえ移した捕囚の民のうち、捕らわれの身から上って来た州の人々である。彼らはエルサレムとユダに帰り、それぞれ自分の町に戻った。
ja.R: これは、捕囚から帰って来たユダの州の人々の名簿です。バビロンの王ネブカドネツァルは、彼らを捕虜として連れて行っていました。今、彼らはエルサレムとユダのほかの地に帰りました。それぞれの家族が、自分の町に戻ったのです。

decisions.choice: the sons of the province: the people of the Persian province of Judah
decisions.reason: Under Persian rule Judah was a small province of the empire. "Sons of the province" means its people, here those who came back from Babylon.

decisions.choice: the captivity of the exile: the people taken to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar took the people of Judah to Babylon in several waves, the last when Jerusalem fell in 587/586 BC (2 Kings 24:14-16; 25:11). Cyrus allowed them to return in 538 BC (Ezra 1:1-4). The verse is nearly word for word the same as Ezra 2:1.

decisions.choice: each to their own town (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The returnees were families, men and women, so Balanced and Readable say "each to their own town". "City" in Hebrew covers small towns as well as cities, and most of these were small towns of Judah (verses 25-38).

decisions.choice: Verses 6-72 keep the Spanish of Ezra 2, changing only what the Hebrew changes
decisions.reason: Nehemiah 7:6-72 is the register of Ezra 2:1-70. The Spanish of Ezra 2 is kept at each level so that readers can compare the two lists; only what the Hebrew of Nehemiah changes is changed (names, numbers, "men of" for "sons of", the order of entries, the gifts of verses 69-71). Where the English Readable of Nehemiah names "the descendants of" once for a group of names, Readable does the same. "Cada uno a su propia ciudad" needs no gender setting.

decisions.choice: the Portuguese of Ezra 2:1, without "E" at the start and without "para a Babilônia"
alternatives: a new wording of the verse
decisions.reason: The verse is nearly word for word Ezra 2:1 (m2), so each level reuses the Portuguese of Ezra 2:1 and of its list (verses 6-72 = Ezra 2:1-70), changing only what Nehemiah's Hebrew changes: here the list opens without "and", and does not say "to Babylon" after "carried into exile", so Literal has no "E" and Balanced says "tinha deportado". "Cada um para a sua cidade" has no gender span, as in Ezra 2:1.

decisions.choice: The list of 7:6-73 keeps the Amharic of Ezra 2 name for name and line for line; here Ezra 2:1's wording without "ወደ ባቢሎን" (to Babylon), which Nehemiah's Hebrew lacks
decisions.reason: Ezra 2 and Nehemiah 7 are the same register. Where Nehemiah's Hebrew differs (a number, a spelling, a name), the Amharic follows Nehemiah and a decision names Ezra 2. Readable follows Nehemiah's English sentences.

decisions.choice: the Hindi of Ezra 2:1 at every level
decisions.reason: Nehemiah 7:6-73 copies the list of Ezra 2, and the Hindi copies its wording, its formulas and its names at every level, changing only where the Hebrew of Nehemiah differs. Here the Hebrew lacks Ezra's "to Babylon" and its opening "and", and says "to Jerusalem and to Judah".

decisions.choice: the wording of Ezra 2:1, without "И" at the start and without "в Вавилон"; "в Иерусалим и в Иуду"
decisions.reason: Nehemiah 7:6-73 is the list of Ezra 2 and reuses its wording at each level. Here the Hebrew has no "and" before "these", no "to Babylon" after the king's name, and repeats "to" before Judah, so the Russian follows it; Balanced "угнал" replaces Ezra's "увёл в Вавилон".

decisions.choice: 7:6-72 keeps the Japanese of Ezra 2:1-70 word for word where the Hebrew agrees (names, "Xの子ら" L / "Xの子孫" B, R, numbers); Nehemiah's own readings (names, numbers, "anshei" for "benei", no "to Babylon" here) are followed where it differs.
decisions.reason: The two registers are one list; a reader comparing them should see only the real differences.

decisions.choice: the list of verses 6-72 worded as in Ezra 2, with the names Nehemiah's list spells differently given their own forms
decisions.reason: The two lists are one register copied twice; matching wording lets a reader set them side by side, while names like Binnui, Hariph and Sia follow the Hebrew of this book, as the English does.

decisions.choice: twelve leaders of the first return; this Nehemiah and Mordecai are not the well-known men of those names
decisions.reason: Zerubbabel, of David's line, and Jeshua the high priest led the first return (Ezra 3:2; Haggai 1:1). The Nehemiah and Mordecai named here lived about ninety years before Nehemiah son of Hacaliah, who writes this memoir, and Mordecai here is probably not Esther's cousin. Twelve names may stand for the twelve tribes. Ezra 2:2 gives eleven names, without Nahamani, and spells some differently (Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mispar, Rehum).

decisions.choice: the number of the men of the people of Israel: the count of the lay families
decisions.reason: The heading introduces the lay Israelites (verses 8-38), listed first by family and then by home town; the priests, Levites and temple servants follow (verses 39-60).

decisions.choice: from each family and town (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable adds these words to show how the list that follows is arranged.

decisions.choice: Zorobabel, Jesua, Neemias, Mardoqueu, Bilsã, Bigvai, Baaná as Ezra 2:2; Azarias, Raamias, Naamani, Misperete, Neum where Nehemiah's names differ
alternatives: Seraías, Reelaías, Mispar, Reum (the forms of Ezra 2:2)
decisions.reason: The names the two lists share keep the forms of Ezra 2:2 in Portuguese. Where Nehemiah's Hebrew has another name (Azariah for Seraiah, Raamiah for Reelaiah, Mispereth for Mispar, Nehum for Rehum) or an extra one (Nahamani, the twelfth leader), Portuguese writes Nehemiah's name, so that the reader sees the difference the Hebrew has. The new forms follow the spelling rules of Ezra 2:3 and are uncertain.

decisions.choice: Ezra 2:2's Amharic with Nehemiah's names: "ዓዛርያስ" (Azariah, as Ezra 7:1) for Seraiah, "ረዕምያ" (Raamiah) for Reelaiah, "ናሐማኒ" (Nahamani, not in Ezra), "ሚስፔሬት" (Mispereth) for Mispar, "ነሑም" (Nehum) for Rehum
decisions.reason: Nehemiah's Hebrew names twelve leaders and spells four of Ezra's eleven differently; the Amharic follows Nehemiah.

decisions.choice: "अजर्याह", "रामयाह", "नहमानी", "मिस्पेरेत", "नहूम"
decisions.reason: Where the Hebrew names differ from Ezra 2:2 the Hindi follows Nehemiah: Azariah (अजर्याह, the form of 1 Chronicles) for Ezra's Seraiah (सरायाह), Raamiah (रामयाह) for Reelaiah (रेलायाह), Mispereth (मिस्पेरेत) for Mispar (मिस्पार), Nehum (नहूम) for Rehum (रहूम), and Nahamani (नहमानी), whom Ezra does not have. The other names keep the forms of Ezra 2:2.

decisions.choice: "Азария", "Раамия", "Нахамани" (indeclinable), "Мисфереф", "Нехум"
decisions.reason: Ezra 2:2 has Seraiah ("Сераия"), Reelaiah ("Реелаия"), Mispar ("Мисфар") and Rehum ("Рехум") and lacks Nahamani; Nehemiah's Hebrew has Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mispereth and Nehum, so these take their own forms, made as Ezra's are ("Азария" as elsewhere in Nehemiah). The other names keep the forms of Ezra 2:2.

decisions.choice: Names as Ezra 2:2 where the Hebrew agrees; Nehemiah's own forms: Azariah "アザルヤ" (Ezra Seraiah), Raamiah "ラアムヤ" (Reelaiah), Nahamani "ナハマニ" (not in Ezra), Mispereth "ミスペレト" (Mispar), Nehum "ネフム" (Rehum).
decisions.reason: Each list keeps its own Hebrew spelling.

decisions.choice: the sons of Parosh: the members of the family of Parosh
decisions.reason: "Sons of" here means descendants, the family that traces its line to one ancestor, men, women and children together. Families are listed by the founder's name; the family of Parosh appears again in Ezra 8:3; 10:25; Nehemiah 3:25; 10:15. Its number is the same as in Ezra 2:3.

decisions.choice: [the] sons of (Literal); the descendants of (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: In the lists, Balanced and Readable say "the descendants of" for a family named after its ancestor, and "the people of" where the name is a town (verses 25, 36-38). Literal keeps "sons of" to show the Hebrew form. Numbers above ninety-nine are written as numerals.

decisions.choice: os filhos de X: N (L); os descendentes de X: N (B, R)
decisions.reason: The formula Ezra 2:3 sets in Portuguese for this list and its repeat here: "os filhos de" at Literal, "os descendentes de" at Balanced and Readable, "o povo de" before a town (verses 25, 36-38) and "os homens de" where the Hebrew says "men", with a colon before the count. Readable follows the English Readable in making each line a sentence.

decisions.choice: the numbers Nehemiah's Hebrew gives; round numbers in words, long counts in figures
alternatives: Ezra's numbers where the lists differ
decisions.reason: Each count is Nehemiah's own, even where Ezra 2 differs (verses 10-62; the meaning decisions name each difference); only the way of writing them is Ezra's: counts under a hundred and round tens, hundreds and thousands in words, longer counts in figures with a point for thousands (2.172).

decisions.choice: Ezra 2:3's formula: "የፋሮስ ልጆች፣ 2,172፤" (Literal), "የፋሮስ ዘሮች" (Balanced, Readable); a town's "sons" "ልጆች" (Literal) / "ሰዎች" (Balanced, Readable); "the men of" "የ... ሰዎች". Numbers follow Nehemiah's Hebrew wherever they differ from Ezra 2
decisions.reason: Readable ends each line with a full stop, as the English Readable of Nehemiah 7 does.

decisions.choice: "X के पुत्र" (Literal); "X के वंशज" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The list formula of Ezra 2, one per level: Literal keeps "sons", Balanced and Readable say वंशज, which is what the phrase means and includes the women. Numbers under a hundred are words and larger ones figures, as in the English; below a lakh the figures are the same in Indian and international grouping.

decisions.choice: "сыновья X, N;" (L); "потомки X — N;" (B, R), as Ezra 2
alternatives: "The descendants of X: N." as separate sentences at Readable
decisions.reason: Nehemiah 7:6-73 copies the list formulas of Ezra 2 at each level, so the two lists read alike; Readable keeps Ezra's list lines instead of the English Readable's separate sentences. Names keep their Ezra 2 forms unless the Hebrew name differs, and numbers follow Nehemiah's Hebrew (the meaning decisions give Ezra's figures).

decisions.choice: benei X "Xの子ら" (L), "Xの子孫" (B, R); a town "Xの子ら" (L), "Xの人々" (B, R); anshei X "Xの男たち" every level; counts in kanji, "[人]" supplied at L, as Ezra 2.
decisions.reason: R keeps the list form of B, as in Ezra 2, rather than the English R colon form.

decisions.choice: of Jeshua, of Kadmiel, of the sons of Hodevah: the Levite families of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of Hodevah's line
alternatives: the sons of Jeshua, that is, of Kadmiel
decisions.reason: The repeated "of" lists Jeshua and Kadmiel as two Levite heads (as Ezra 2:40 joins them with "and"; compare Ezra 3:9), both counted under the line of Hodevah. Ezra 2:40 spells that name Hodaviah.

decisions.choice: seventy-four: very few Levites came back
decisions.reason: Only seventy-four Levites returned, against over four thousand priests (verses 39-42), the same small number as in Ezra 2:40. Ezra later had trouble finding Levites willing to come (Ezra 8:15-19).

decisions.choice: "ሆዴዋ" (Hodevah) as Nehemiah spells the name; Ezra 2:40 has "ሆዳውያ" (Hodaviah). Literal keeps "of Kadmiel" as its own phrase ("ከቀድምኤል"), as Nehemiah's Hebrew has it
decisions.reason: Nehemiah writes "of Kadmiel" where Ezra has "and Kadmiel"; Balanced and Readable keep Ezra's wording, as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: "होदवा"; "कदमीएल के" (L)
decisions.reason: Nehemiah 7:43 has Hodevah (होदवा) where Ezra 2:40 has Hodaviah (होदव्याह): a different spelling of the name in the Hebrew, so a different Hindi form. Nehemiah also says "of Kadmiel" where Ezra says "and Kadmiel", which Literal follows; Balanced and Readable keep Ezra's wording, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Годева"; "от Кадмиила" (L)
decisions.reason: Ezra 2:40 has Hodaviah ("из сыновей Годавии") and "Jeshua and Kadmiel"; Nehemiah's Hebrew spells the name Hodevah and says "of Kadmiel", which Literal follows as Ezra 2:16 follows "of Hezekiah" ("от Езекии").

decisions.choice: Hodevah "ホデワ" (Ezra 2:40 Hodaviah "ホダウヤ"); Kadmiel "カドミエル".
decisions.reason: Nehemiah's Hebrew spelling.

decisions.choice: the gatekeepers: the families who guarded the temple gates
decisions.reason: The gatekeepers kept watch at the temple gates and storerooms (1 Chronicles 9:17-27). Shallum, Talmon and Akkub appear as gatekeeper families there and in 11:19; 12:25. Ezra 2:42 gives 139.

decisions.choice: the descendants of Shallum, Ater, ... (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "the descendants of" once for the whole list instead of before every name; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: "Los porteros:" for the heading
decisions.reason: Nehemiah's heading is "the gatekeepers", where Ezra 2:42 has "the sons of the gatekeepers" and adds "all of them"; the Spanish follows the Hebrew of Nehemiah.

decisions.choice: "Mabawabu" (L, B), "walinzi wa malango" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Ezra 2:42; the heading here is "the gatekeepers", not "the sons of the gatekeepers".

decisions.choice: Os porteiros (L)
decisions.reason: Ezra 2:42 reads "the sons of the gatekeepers" and adds "all of them"; Nehemiah's Hebrew has only "the gatekeepers" and the count, so Literal follows it here and the rest of the line keeps Ezra's Portuguese.

decisions.choice: "በር ጠባቂዎቹ፦" (the gatekeepers) and "138" with no "ሁሉም" (all), as Nehemiah's Hebrew; Ezra 2:42 has "the sons of the gatekeepers ... all of them 139"
decisions.reason: Nehemiah's Hebrew lacks "the sons of" and "all"; the names keep Ezra 2:42's Amharic.

decisions.choice: "द्वारपाल:" with no "सब" or "कुल"
decisions.reason: Nehemiah says "the gatekeepers" where Ezra 2:42 says "the sons of the gatekeepers" (द्वारपालों के पुत्र / के वंशज), and it has no word for "all" before the number, so the Hindi drops Ezra's सब [मिलाकर] and कुल.

decisions.choice: "Привратники:"; no "всего"
decisions.reason: Ezra 2:42 begins "the sons of the gatekeepers" and ends "all of them, 139"; Nehemiah's Hebrew says "the gatekeepers" and has no "all", so the heading and the total follow it.

decisions.choice: the Nethinim: the temple servants, literally "the given ones"
decisions.reason: The word means "those given": people given to the temple to serve the Levites (Ezra 8:20). They did manual work at the sanctuary. Some of their families may go back to foreigners attached to Israel, such as the Gibeonites who became woodcutters and water carriers for the house of God (Joshua 9:23-27), and several names in this list (verses 46-56) are not Israelite in form.

decisions.choice: the Nethinim (Literal); the temple servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew title; Balanced and Readable say what these people were. In verses 46-59 Readable also says "the descendants of" once for each group of names instead of before every name.

decisions.choice: os servidores do templo (every level)
decisions.reason: As Ezra 2:43 in Portuguese, for Ezra-Nehemiah: the "given ones" (m1) are named by their work at every level, since the Portuguese form of the Hebrew title would mean nothing to most readers; the English Literal keeps the title. Readable says "os descendentes de" once for each line, as the English Readable does in verses 46-59.

decisions.choice: Readable names each group's families once before "ዘሮች" (the descendants of), with a full stop, as the English Readable does in 7:46-59
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep Ezra 2:43-57's line "የ... ልጆች / ዘሮች፣" for each name.

decisions.choice: "मन्दिर के सेवक" at every level
decisions.reason: As in Ezra 2:43, the Hindi names the Nethinim by their work at every level, though the English Literal keeps the Hebrew word. Readable keeps "के वंशज" before each name, as in Ezra 2.

decisions.choice: Nephishesim: the reading of the margin
decisions.reason: The name is written in the text in a slightly different form from the one the scribes' note in the margin gives; the marginal form is followed. Ezra 2:50 has a similar name, Nephisim, after the family of Asnah, which is not in this list. Meunim may be descendants of the Meunites, a people south of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:41; 2 Chronicles 26:7).

decisions.choice: "ነፊሽሲም" for Nephishesim, the reading of the margin; Ezra 2:50 has "ነፊሲም" (Nephusim)

decisions.choice: "नपीशसीम"
decisions.reason: Nehemiah 7:52 has Nephishesim (नपीशसीम, the name as read) where Ezra 2:50 has Nephusim (नपूसीम): a different form of the name. Ezra's Asnah (अस्ना, 2:50) is not in Nehemiah's list.

decisions.choice: "Нефишесим"; no "Асна"
decisions.reason: Ezra 2:50 has Asnah ("Асна") before Meunim and Nephusim ("Нефусим"); Nehemiah's Hebrew has no Asnah and reads Nephishesim (the margin's reading).

decisions.choice: the sons of the slaves of Solomon: descendants of the forced laborers of Solomon's reign
decisions.reason: Solomon made the peoples left in the land from before Israel into a labor force (1 Kings 9:20-21). Their descendants kept a place among the temple staff and are counted with the temple servants (verse 60). The word means servants who were owned, not hired. Ezra 2:55 has Hassophereth and Peruda for the second and third names.

decisions.choice: slaves (Literal); servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere, Literal keeps "slaves" and Balanced and Readable say "servants", since the group is named by an old status and the list is not about slavery as such; the meaning decision says what their position was.

decisions.choice: escravos (L); servos (B, R)
decisions.reason: As Ezra 2:55 in Portuguese and the English (r-en-1): the Old Testament terms' rule for this word, "escravo" at Literal and "servo" at Balanced and Readable, since the group is named by an old status (m1).

decisions.choice: "ሶፌሬት" (Sophereth) and "ፍሪዳ" (Perida); Ezra 2:55 has "ሐሶፌሬት" (Hassophereth) and "ፍሩዳ" (Peruda). "ባሪያዎች" (Literal) / "አገልጋዮች" (Balanced, Readable) for Solomon's slaves, as Ezra 2:55
decisions.reason: Nehemiah's Hebrew has no article on Sophereth and spells Perida with i.

decisions.choice: "सोपेरेत", "परीदा"
decisions.reason: Nehemiah 7:57 has Sophereth (सोपेरेत) and Perida (परीदा) where Ezra 2:55 has Hassophereth (हस्सोपेरेत) and Peruda (परूदा): the Hebrew drops the article of the first and spells the second differently.

decisions.choice: "दास" at every level
decisions.reason: As in Ezra 2:55: Hindi दास covers both slave and servant, so the English Balanced and Readable "servants" needs no other word.

decisions.choice: "Софереф", "Ферида"
decisions.reason: Ezra 2:55 has Hassophereth, with the article ("Гассоферефа"), and Peruda ("Феруды"); Nehemiah's Hebrew has Sophereth and Perida. "Раб" stays at every level, as in Ezra 2:55.

decisions.choice: 'avdei Shelomoh "ソロモンの奴隷たち" (L), "ソロモンのしもべたち" (B, R), as Ezra 2:55; Sophereth "ソフェレト", Perida "ペリダ" (Ezra "ハソフェレト", "ペルダ").
decisions.reason: As the English levels; Nehemiah's spellings.

decisions.choice: "አሞን" (Amon, written as the king's name in 2 Kings 21); Ezra 2:57 has "አሚ" (Ami)

decisions.choice: "आमोन"
decisions.reason: Nehemiah 7:59 has Amon (आमोन, the form of the king in 1 Chronicles 3:14) where Ezra 2:57 has Ami (आमी): a different name in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "Амон"
decisions.reason: Ezra 2:57 has Ami ("Ами"); Nehemiah's Hebrew has Amon, in the form of the king's name in this translation.

records.literal_gloss: And these [are] the ones coming up from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Kerub, Addon, and Immer; and not they were able to declare [the] house of their fathers and their seed, whether from Israel they [were]:

en.L: And these [are] the ones who came up from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Kerub, Addon and Immer, and they were not able to declare the house of their fathers or their descent, whether they [were] from Israel:
en.B: These are the ones who came up from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Kerub, Addon and Immer, but they could not show their family or their descent, whether they were from Israel:
en.R: Some people came back from the towns of Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Kerub, Addon and Immer. But they could not prove which family they belonged to, or that their ancestors were Israelites.

es.L: Y estos [son] los que subieron de Tel-mela, Tel-harsa, Querub, Adón e Imer, pero no pudieron mostrar su casa paterna ni su descendencia, si [eran] de Israel:
es.B: Estos son los que subieron de Tel-mela, Tel-harsa, Querub, Adón e Imer, pero no pudieron demostrar su familia ni su linaje, si pertenecían a Israel:
es.R: Algunos vinieron de las ciudades de Tel-mela, Tel-harsa, Querub, Adón e Imer. Pero no pudieron probar a qué familia pertenecían, ni que sus antepasados eran israelitas.

fr.L: Et voici ceux qui montèrent de Tel-Mélah, Tel-Harsha, Keroub, Addôn et Immer, mais ils ne purent pas indiquer la maison de leurs pères et leur descendance, s’ils [étaient] d’Israël :
fr.B: Voici ceux qui montèrent de Tel-Mélah, Tel-Harsha, Keroub, Addôn et Immer, sans pouvoir indiquer leur famille ni leur ascendance, pour montrer s’ils appartenaient à Israël :
fr.R: Des gens sont revenus des villes de Tel-Mélah, Tel-Harsha, Keroub, Addôn et Immer. Mais ils n’ont pas pu prouver à quelle famille ils appartenaient, ni que leurs ancêtres étaient israélites.

sw.L: Na hawa [ndio] waliopanda kutoka Tel-mela, Tel-harsha, Kerubu, Adoni na Imeri, lakini hawakuweza kuonyesha nyumba ya baba zao na uzao wao, kama walikuwa wa Israeli:
sw.B: Hawa ndio waliopanda kutoka Tel-mela, Tel-harsha, Kerubu, Adoni na Imeri, ingawa hawakuweza kuonyesha jamaa zao wala ukoo wao, kama walikuwa wa Israeli:
sw.R: Watu wengine walirudi kutoka miji ya Tel-mela, Tel-harsha, Kerubu, Adoni na Imeri. Lakini hawakuweza kuthibitisha walikuwa wa jamaa gani, wala kwamba babu zao walikuwa Waisraeli.

vi.L: Và đây [là] những người đã đi lên từ Tên-Mê-la, Tên-Hạt-sa, Kê-rúp, A-đôn và Y-mê, nhưng họ không thể chỉ ra nhà tổ phụ của họ và dòng dõi của họ, xem họ có thuộc về Y-sơ-ra-ên không:

ko.L: 그리고 이들은 델멜라, 델하르사, 그룹, 앗돈, 임멜에서 올라온 자들인데, 그들은 자기 조상의 집과 자기 혈통이 이스라엘에 속했는지를 밝힐 수 없었다.

ko.R: 델멜라, 델하르사, 그룹, 앗돈, 임멜 같은 곳에서 돌아온 사람들도 있었다. 그러나 그들은 자기가 어느 집안에 속하는지, 자기 조상이 이스라엘 사람인지 증명하지 못했다.

pt.L: E estes [são] os que subiram de Tel-Melá, Tel-Harsa, Querube, Adom [e] Imer, mas não puderam mostrar a casa dos seus pais e a sua descendência, se eles [eram] de Israel:
pt.B: Estes são os que subiram de Tel-Melá, Tel-Harsa, Querube, Adom e Imer, mas não puderam mostrar a sua família nem a sua descendência, se pertenciam a Israel:

am.L: ከቴልሜላ፣ ከቴልሐርሳ፣ ከክሩብ፣ ከአዶንና ከኢሜር የወጡትም እነዚህ ናቸው፤ ከእስራኤል ይሁኑ እንደ ሆነ የአባቶቻቸውን ቤትና ዘራቸውን ማሳየት አልቻሉም፦

am.R: አንዳንድ ሰዎች ከቴልሜላ፣ ከቴልሐርሳ፣ ከክሩብ፣ ከአዶንና ከኢሜር ከተሞች ተመለሱ። ነገር ግን የየትኛው ቤተሰብ ወገን እንደ ሆኑ ወይም አባቶቻቸው እስራኤላውያን እንደ ነበሩ ማረጋገጥ አልቻሉም።

ja.L: そして、テル・メラ、テル・ハルシャ、ケルブ、アドン、イメルから上って来た者たちで、自分たちがイスラエルの出であるかどうか、その父祖の家とその子孫を示すことができなかった者たちは次のとおりである。

ja.R: テル・メラ、テル・ハルシャ、ケルブ、アドン、イメルという町から来た人々もいましたが、自分たちの家族がイスラエルの出であることを証明できませんでした。それは次の人々です。

uk.L: І оце ті, що піднялися з Тел-Мелаху, Тел-Харші, Керуву, Аддону та Іммеру, але не змогли показати дому своїх батьків і свого насіння, чи вони з Ізраїля [були]:
uk.B: Ось ті, що прийшли з Тел-Мелаху, Тел-Харші, Керуву, Аддону та Іммеру, але не могли довести свого роду і походження, чи належать вони до Ізраїля:
uk.R: Деякі люди повернулися з міст Тел-Мелах, Тел-Харша, Керув, Аддон та Іммер. Але вони не могли довести, до якого роду належать і чи їхні предки були ізраїльтянами.

decisions.choice: Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Kerub, Addon, Immer: places in Babylonia where exiles had lived
decisions.reason: "Tel" means a mound, the site of an old ruined town; the exiles were settled at places like these (Ezekiel 3:15, Tel-abib). Ezra 2:59 spells the fourth name Addan.

decisions.choice: declare the house of their fathers and their seed: prove from records which family they came from
decisions.reason: To belong to Israel, and to hold land or serve as priests, a family had to show its line of descent. These families had no record to show it (verse 64). They were not sent away; they are counted with the rest (verse 66).

decisions.choice: "አዶን" (Addon); Ezra 2:59 has "አዳን" (Addan). Literal drops Ezra's "ነገር ግን" (but), as Nehemiah's English Literal says "and"
decisions.reason: Nehemiah's Hebrew spells the name Addon; the other names keep Ezra 2:59's Amharic.

decisions.choice: "अद्दोन"; "और इम्मेर" (L)
decisions.reason: Nehemiah 7:61 has Addon (अद्दोन) where Ezra 2:59 has Addan (अद्दान): a different spelling in the Hebrew. Tel Melah, Tel Harsha and Kerub are spelled as in Ezra (तेल-मेलह, तेल-हर्शा, करूब), since the Hebrew is the same; Nehemiah has "and" before Immer, so Literal does not bracket it.

decisions.choice: "Аддон"; "и Иммера" (L, no brackets)
decisions.reason: Ezra 2:59 has Addan ("Аддана") and no "and" before Immer; Nehemiah's Hebrew has Addon and "and Immer".

decisions.choice: Addon "アドン" (Ezra 2:59 Addan "アダン"); the other places as Ezra: "テル・メラ", "テル・ハルシャ", "ケルブ", "イメル".
decisions.reason: Nehemiah's spelling.

decisions.choice: R as Ezra 2:59-60 R: this sentence ends "それは次の人々です", and 7:62 R lists "デラヤ、トビヤ、ネコダの子孫、合わせて…".
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of 7:61-62 is Ezra 2:59-60 apart from the names and the number, so the Japanese is kept the same; the English R words the link differently.

decisions.reason: The parallel list gives these families 652 (see verse 10). This Tobiah is a family of the first return, not to be confused with Tobiah the Ammonite official who opposed Nehemiah (2:10; 6:17-19).
